item.title: Global Bond Retreat Slows as Decade-High Yields Tempt Investors
item.description: Global bonds clawed back ground as yields near multi-decade highs proved hard for some investors to resist, even as energy prices keep markets on edge.

item.title: Hungary Central Bank Files Police Report on Overpriced Property
item.description: The National Bank of Hungary pressed charges over fresh instances of suspected embezzlement under its previous governor, related to a series of allegedly overpriced property acquisitions.

item.title: Why Bond Yields Surging Around the World (UST)
item.description: Darrell Duffie thinks the Treasury market is far from fixed.

item.title: Schroders Buys Long-Dated Treasuries Citing Attractive Yields
item.description: British asset manager Schroders Plc has bought more of longer-dated US Treasuries, saying yields have nearly peaked after the recent selloff.

item.title: Air India Closes in on $1.1 Billion Financial Aid From Owners
item.description: Air India Ltd. is close to securing 100 billion rupees ($1.1 billion) in financial aid from its owners Tata Sons Pvt. and Singapore Airlines Ltd., according to people familiar with the matter, as the carrier grapples with the fallout from a turbulent year.

item.title: Billionaire Birla Unit’s Buyout Loan Draws $2.5 Billion in Bids
item.description: A unit of Indian billionaire Kumar Mangalam Birla’s conglomerate has received as much as 240 billion rupees ($2.5 billion) in commitments from at least four banks for an acquisition loan, 70% more than what it was planning for, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: BOJ Is Said to Favor Quarter-Point Hike, Flexible on Future Path
item.description: The Bank of Japan is leaning toward raising its benchmark interest rate by a quarter point this month in response to upward price risks, while leaving open the possibility of accelerating the pace of hikes thereafter, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: European Stocks Advance as Elliott Stake Lifts Deutsche Telekom
item.description: European stocks edged higher on Thursday as oil and bond markets stabilized, while Deutsche Telekom AG gained on news that activist investor Elliott Investment Management has built a sizeable stake.

item.title: Turkey Prices Cool Further in August, Raising Rate-Cut Prospect
item.description: Turkish inflation slowed more than expected last month, strengthening the case for an interest-rate cut as early as September.

item.title: Malaysia Holds Key Rate and Signals Hawkish Pivot; Swaps Climb
item.description: Malaysia’s central bank extended its interest rate pause but tweaked its monetary policy statement to remove a reference to its stance as being “appropriate,” in a possible signal that borrowing costs could rise.

item.title: Crest Nicholson Now Sees Full-Year Loss on UK Housing Slump
item.description: Crest Nicholson Holdings Plc reversed previous guidance for a modest profit this year and now expects to make a loss thanks to a subdued housing market and lackluster pricing. Shares plunged.

item.title: Swiss Inflation Rate Jumps to the Highest Level in Two Years
item.description: Swiss inflation accelerated far more than analysts anticipated to the fastest pace since September 2024, suggesting a weaker franc is feeding through to the economy.

item.title: K-Pop Billionaire Bang Referred to Prosecutors, Yonhap Says
item.description: South Korean police shared with prosecutors the findings of a long-running investigation into BTS agency Hybe Co. founder Bang Si-hyuk over allegations he misled investors ahead of the company’s 2020 listing.

item.title: Russians See New Allure in Cash as War Hits Closer to Home
item.description: Russians are increasingly turning to cash as the war hits closer to home, a shift that is reversing a years-long decline in physical currency use and underscores growing anxiety about the future.

item.title: Merz to Meet ECB Officials Before Berlin Rate Meeting Next Week
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz will meet European Central Bank officials next week in Berlin as they convene there for an interest-rate decision that coincides with growing speculation over President Christine Lagarde’s future.

item.title: Asia’s Economies Avert Energy Shock Via Fiscal Buffers, AI Boom
item.description: Asia’s economies from India to Malaysia and Australia defied all worst-case scenarios to post solid growth last quarter, as governments moved quickly to secure energy supplies and tapped relatively healthy balance sheets to cushion households.

item.title: Danske Sees Highest Danish GDP Growth Since 2021 on Novo Boost
item.description: Surging pharmaceutical exports led by Novo Nordisk A/S are set to propel Denmark’s economy to its strongest pace in five years and continue fueling the expansion in 2027, according to the country’s largest lender.

item.title: Thailand Must Double Per-Capita Growth to Reach Rich Goal, World Bank Says
item.description: Thailand needs to more than double the pace of per-capita economic growth to achieve its goal of high-income status by 2037, according to the World Bank, a target it says is within reach if Bangkok pushes through reforms to boost productivity and competitiveness.

item.title: One in Three Firms Backed by UK Covid Fund Are Now Insolvent
item.description: More than a third of companies backed by the UK government under a rescue program during Covid have gone bust, costing the taxpayer £423 million ($571 million).

item.title: Japan’s 30-Year Bond Sale Demand Stronger Than 12-Month Average
item.description: Japan’s 30-year government bond auction Thursday saw stronger demand than the 12-month average as elevated yields underpinned buying.

item.title: Dry Bulk Shipping Rates Surge on Tight Capesize Vessel Supply
item.description: A key measure of bulk-shipping rates has touched a two-year high and risks climbing further, according to analysts, as bad weather crimps the availability of Capesize vessels just as exporters ramp up delivery.

item.title: India’s Rupee Gains as RBI Measures Bring in Bumper $136 Billion
item.description: India’s rupee gained as the central bank garnered $136 billion under its capital-raising measures, far exceeding expectations and further boosting its war chest to defend the currency.

item.title: HDFC Bank Is at Risk of Losing Its Top Nifty Spot to Rival ICICI
item.description: HDFC Bank Ltd. is barely holding on to its position as the most influential stock on India’s equity benchmark as a leadership upheaval and governance concerns deepen a selloff.

item.title: Base Metals Gain Ground as Trump Says Iran Attacks Will Be Brief
item.description: Metals advanced after President Donald Trump said that a new wave of US attacks on Iran would likely be short-lived, easing concerns about further escalation in the region that hurt prices on Wednesday.

item.title: Yen Traders Brace for Holiday Intervention Risk Around BOJ
item.description: Yen traders are on heightened alert for possible intervention around the Bank of Japan’s upcoming policy meeting, with a three-day holiday following the decision offering authorities an opportunity to act in thinner trading.

item.title: HDFC Bank’s Nifty Crown Under Threat From ICICI Bank After CEO Exit
item.description: Lender’s shares have tumbled 29% this year, their worst showing relative to the Nifty Bank gauge since 2003.

item.title: Singapore Ruling on Bankrupt Indonesian Firm May Open Recovery Path for Others
item.description: A Singapore court’s landmark decision allowing administrators of bankrupt Indonesian textile maker PT Sri Rejeki Isman to pursue assets in the city-state may open a new route to recoveries for investors in other insolvent Indonesian firms with links to Singapore.

item.title: ByteDance Gets $30 Billion Loan, Asia’s Second-Largest This Year
item.description: ByteDance Ltd., the developer of TikTok, has secured a $29.6 billion loan, according to people familiar with the matter, in Asia’s second-largest dollar-denominated borrowing this year.

item.title: Vietnam Trade Gap Narrows to $113 Million; Inflation Faster
item.description: Vietnam’s trade deficit drastically narrowed in August as the government pushes to reduce the nation’s reliance on imported components for its booming manufacturing sector.
